Skiplist for the corpus freshness check. Two buckets:
  * "missing" — case names JS has and Python deliberately doesn't. Use when JS adds a case for a feature Python doesn't (yet) support.
  * "drift"   — case names where Python deliberately keeps a different body from JS. Use sparingly — body-drift on a shared case is usually a bug.
Extras (Python has, JS doesn't) are reported but never fail CI, so they don't need an entry here.
Add a brief reason in `_reasons` whenever you add an entry so future maintainers know why.

feature: CB rule with empty contexts (explore) buckets on marginal weights with fallback leaf -1
CB rule with no contexts key falls back to marginal weights (fallback leaf -1)
CB rule with empty contexts uses marginal weights (fallback leaf -1)
CB rule with empty contexts is overridden by forced variation like a normal experiment

_reasons._example_missing: evalCondition::case name -> short reason (e.g. 'tests $someOperator that Python doesn't implement yet').
_reasons._example_drift: evalCondition::case name -> short reason (e.g. 'JS shipped a behavioral change in case X; Python intentionally kept the prior expectation pending review').
_reasons.feature::CB rule with empty contexts (ex: contextual bandit rules (spec 0.8.0: contextualBandits payload + contextualVariations) are not implemented in the Python SDK yet
_reasons.feature::CB rule with no contexts key fa: contextual bandit rules (spec 0.8.0: contextualBandits payload + contextualVariations) are not implemented in the Python SDK yet
_reasons.feature::CB rule with empty contexts use: contextual bandit rules (spec 0.8.0: contextualBandits payload + contextualVariations) are not implemented in the Python SDK yet
_reasons.feature::CB rule with empty contexts is: contextual bandit rules (spec 0.8.0: contextualBandits payload + contextualVariations) are not implemented in the Python SDK yet
